title: Snow globe: electrophoretic nanoparticle position stores the bit
idea: Random stimulus 'snow globe' forced onto memory: a 5 nm charged oxide nanoparticle is sealed in a 30 nm liquid-filled nanocavity between two plates; a +/-1 V write drives it to the top or bottom by electrophoresis, and a coplanar sense electrode reads its position as a capacitance shift. The bit is where a particle sits, not how much charge remains, so junction leakage cannot erase it.
why: Removes refresh (fact 3, ~46 fJ/bit and 10-20% bandwidth) and the high-AR capacitor (fact 1); nothing wears, so endurance is unlimited; claimed ~10x lower idle power if nanoconfined transit is <50 ns.

title: Light switch: snap-through buckled nanobeam as a bistable bit
idea: Stimulus 'wall light switch' (two detents, no power to hold) -> a 200 nm compressively pre-stressed TiN or SiN beam is buckled up or down over a sense electrode; an electrostatic pulse on the opposite electrode snaps it through, and the up/down position changes cell capacitance ~3x for read. Built-in stress, not charge, holds the state.
why: Zero static leakage so no refresh (fact 3); no capacitor charge wall (fact 1); stacks in BEOL tiers without a lateral transistor (fact 2); ~20 ns snap at GHz resonance.

title: Abacus bead: electron packet shuttled between twin floating islands
idea: Stimulus 'abacus' (a bead slides, nothing is added or removed) -> each cell has two oxide-isolated floating nano-islands joined by a gated tunnel barrier; writing moves a fixed packet of ~5,000 electrons left or right, and a differential sense amp compares the two islands. Total charge is conserved, so substrate/junction leakage disappears and common-mode drift cancels while the signal doubles.
why: Doubles sense margin per stored electron, so Cs can halve (~5 fF -> ~2.5 fF), cutting pillar AR from ~70:1 to ~35:1 (fact 1) and relaxing refresh because only intra-cell differential leakage matters (fact 3).

title: Thermos flask: vacuum-isolated node behind a zero-leakage nanorelay
idea: Stimulus 'thermos' (vacuum stops heat leaking) -> replace the access transistor with an electrostatic nanorelay whose contact opens a 5 nm vacuum gap, and wrap the storage node in a sealed vacuum cavity, so the off path has no semiconductor junction or channel to leak through. Stored charge decays only by field emission across the gap, negligible at 1 V.
why: Kills the <=13 fA leakage tail (fact 3): retention moves from 64 ms to minutes, cutting refresh energy and bandwidth loss >100x; relay pitch is not bound by transistor EUV layers (fact 4).

title: Mousetrap: strain-cocked ferroelastic twin variant holds the bit
idea: Stimulus 'cocked mousetrap' (stored elastic energy, two positions) -> a 20 nm ferroelastic perovskite pillar (e.g., LaCoO3-type) holds one of two twin orientations; a piezoelectric collar applies a ~1 ns shear pulse to flip the twin, and the variants' anisotropic resistivity (~2x) is read nondestructively along the pillar.
why: Non-charge storage with no refresh (fact 3) and nondestructive read that removes the restore cycle (fact 8); twin flipping moves no defects or ions, so endurance can be very high.

title: Champagne fizz: electrolytic nanobubble toggles nanochannel resistance
idea: Stimulus 'champagne bubble' -> a 15 nm nanochannel holds dilute aqueous electrolyte between two carbon electrodes; a short pulse electrolyzes a few thousand molecules into an insulating H2 nanobubble that pins in a hydrophobic pocket (bit 1), and a reverse pulse recombines and dissolves it (bit 0). Read is a 0.1 V resistance probe with >100x contrast.
why: A bit with no stored charge and no filament defects (unlike ReRAM): attacks refresh (fact 3) and the capacitor wall (fact 1); huge on/off ratio allows ~4F^2 cells.

title: Pendulum clock: parametron phase bit sustained by one shared pump
idea: Stimulus 'pendulum clock' -> each cell is a GHz nanomechanical or LC resonator pumped parametrically at twice its frequency, so it can only oscillate at phase 0 or pi (Goto's 1950s parametron shrunk to NEMS); one global pump tone sustains every bit at once. Read compares phase with a reference; write injects a small seed signal as the local pump restarts.
why: Replaces row-by-row refresh with continuous collective sustain that steals no bandwidth (fact 3); no capacitor (fact 1); high-Q resonators need only ~aW per bit to stay alive.

title: Ice cube tray: nanopore fills or drains, 80x capacitance swing
idea: Stimulus 'ice cube tray' (each cell full or empty) -> each cell is a 10 nm hydrophobic nanopore connected to a sealed water reservoir; such pores are bistable (liquid-filled vs vapor-filled), and an electrowetting pulse fills one while a reverse pulse triggers capillary drying. Water (k~80) vs vapor (k~1) changes pore capacitance ~80x, a giant read signal.
why: Huge per-cell signal removes the 5 fF capacitor requirement (fact 1); the state is thermodynamic, not leaking charge, so no refresh (fact 3); planar cell with no deep etch (fact 4).

title: Zipper: sliding bilayer registry flips polarization by one atom-step
idea: Stimulus 'zipper' (two rows of teeth interlock in one of two registries) -> bilayer hBN or MoS2 stacked AB or BA; a vertical field slides one layer by one bond length, flipping the interfacial polarization, read by tunnel current through the bilayer. Switching is a shear slide, not ion or defect motion, so fatigue is minimal.
why: Sub-nm nonvolatile storage element switching below 0.5 V breaks the CV^2 voltage floor (fact 10) and removes refresh (fact 3); transferable sheets stack as BEOL tiers (fact 2).

title: Conveyor-belt sushi: bits ride recirculating gigahertz phonon loops
idea: Stimulus 'sushi conveyor' -> store data as acoustic pulses circulating in short on-chip AlN acoustic loops (64 bits per ~1.3 ns, ~10 um loop), regenerated by a tiny amplifier each lap, like a mercury delay line made micro. Sound is ~10^5x slower than light, so a micron-scale loop holds a cache line with no capacitor or access transistor.
why: Capacitor-free, transistor-light storage with no leakage tail (fact 3) built on mature-node, EUV-free lines (fact 4); periphery shrinks to one amplifier per 64 bits (fact 7); density is lower, so it targets capital-light capacity tiers.

title: Lava lamp: VO2 nanodot parked inside its Mott hysteresis loop
idea: Stimulus 'lava lamp' (a heat-driven state that persists) -> a 20 nm VO2 nanodot, Cr-doped and strained to widen its thermal hysteresis to ~15 K, sits on a bias heater rail holding it mid-loop; a ~5 ns current pulse flips it metallic, a cooling pulse resets it insulating, and the ~100x resistance contrast is read nondestructively.
why: Charge-free state means no leakage refresh (fact 3) and nondestructive read (fact 8); ~4F^2 cell with no capacitor (fact 1).

title: Chameleon: spin-crossover molecules toggle high-spin and low-spin states
idea: Stimulus 'chameleon' (changes color on cue) -> a 10 nm film of an Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover complex with room-temperature thermal hysteresis; a local ns heat or field pulse switches molecules between low-spin and high-spin, changing film permittivity and conductance by ~10-30%, read by a thin-film transistor gated through the film.
why: Intrinsically bistable molecular bit (no refresh, fact 3), solution-processed with no EUV (fact 4), built from earth-abundant iron.

title: Matryoshka doll: lithium ion rattling inside a fullerene cage
idea: Stimulus 'nesting doll' -> Li+@C60 endohedral fullerenes, where the ion sits off-centre in one of several wells inside the cage; a monolayer sits on a FET gate and a field pulse pushes each ion to the 'top' or 'bottom' well, whose dipole shifts the FET threshold. The cage shields the ion from chemistry and moisture.
why: Single-molecule bit (~1 nm^2) with no capacitor (fact 1) and threshold readout that does not destroy the state (fact 8); potential 100x density if room-temperature wells are deep enough.

title: Pop-up toaster: telescoping nested nanotube held extended or retracted
idea: Stimulus 'pop-up toaster' -> a double-walled carbon nanotube whose inner tube slides out of the outer one; an electrostatic pull extends it to touch a contact pad (bit 1), and the van der Waals retraction force plus a reverse pulse pulls it back (bit 0). Read is contact current; the shell-in-shell sliding is superlubric, so there is no bending fatigue.
why: Zero-leakage nonvolatile mechanical bit (fact 3) with near-frictionless motion for high endurance; vertical tubes stack in BEOL with no capacitor (facts 1-2).

title: Apollo core rope: toroidal nanomagnet rings with coincident-current selection
idea: Stimulus 'Apollo core memory' -> revive ferrite-core memory at 100 nm: each bit is a closed-flux CoFeB nanoring whose clockwise/counterclockwise circulation flips only where two half-select currents in a crossbar coincide, so no access transistor is needed. Read uses a tunnel junction on one arc of the ring.
why: Removes the access transistor and its leakage tail (fact 3), turns the array into a pure BEOL crossbar stackable in tiers (fact 2), and flux closure gives zero stray field for tight packing.

title: Corrugated cardboard: charge-density-wave domain pattern as switchable bit
idea: Stimulus 'corrugated cardboard' (a frozen periodic ripple) -> a thin 1T-TaS2 flake whose charge-density wave is driven between an insulating commensurate-like state and a hidden metallic domain state by a ps-ns current pulse; resistance changes ~10x and the hidden state persists. Substrate strain is engineered to keep it metastable at operating temperature.
why: Among the fastest known electronic phase switches (ps) at fJ energy (fact 10) with nondestructive read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1).

title: Balloon on sweater: contact-electrified charge tapped onto a pad
idea: Stimulus 'balloon rubbed on a sweater' -> a biased nanocantilever taps a trap-rich dielectric pad (e.g., Si3N4) to deposit or strip a few hundred electrons by contact electrification; the trapped charge gates a sense FET below. No tunnel current crosses an oxide, so there is none of Flash's oxide wear.
why: Nonvolatile charge storage with years of retention and no refresh (fact 3), yet endurance is not limited by tunnel-oxide damage; no storage capacitor (fact 1).

title: Garden hose: conductive ferroelectric domain wall opened or kinked off
idea: Stimulus 'garden hose' (flow on, or kinked off) -> in a thin LiNbO3 or BiFeO3 mesa, a write pulse creates or erases a charged head-to-head domain wall bridging two electrodes; the wall conducts ~1000x more than the bulk, so read is a small nondestructive current and the wall stays put without power.
why: Nondestructive read with no restore (fact 8), no refresh (fact 3), and current-mode read that suits vertical stacking (fact 2).

title: Rubik's cube: octahedral-rotation pattern sets polarization, improper ferroelectric
idea: Stimulus 'Rubik's cube' (twist one block, the whole face changes) -> a hybrid improper ferroelectric (Ca3Ti2O7-type) whose polarization is a by-product of two oxygen-octahedra rotation patterns; switching one rotation flips P at low field with domain walls that do not pin. The film is the storage capacitor in a 1T1C or gain-cell read.
why: Lower coercive voltage than HZO and rotation-mediated, fatigue-resistant switching beat the ~1 V / ~3 V voltage floor (fact 10) while giving nonvolatile, refresh-free storage (fact 3).

title: Janus coin: ferroelectric semiconductor channel that stores and senses itself
idea: Stimulus 'two-faced coin' -> use 2D alpha-In2Se3, a semiconductor whose own lattice polarization can flip, as the transistor channel; the polarization direction sets the threshold, so one device both stores and reads the bit with no capacitor and no separate ferroelectric gate layer.
why: 1T0C cell (~4F^2) removes the capacitor wall (fact 1) and destructive read (fact 8); low-temperature 2D transfer allows stacked tiers (fact 2).

title: Seed bank: national shuttle wafers for wild storage-element candidates
idea: Stimulus 'seed bank' -> a CHIPS-funded 300 mm back-end shuttle where any lab drops a candidate storage stack into a standard 1T1X 1 Mb test array four times a year, with shared ns-pulse testers, 10^15-cycle endurance rigs and open retention-tail data. One-off device papers become array statistics in 6 months.
why: Cuts the time and capital to qualify a new bit element from years and ~$50M to months and ~$100k (capital/time chokepoint), seeding U.S. memory manufacturability.

title: Coffee pod: storage-element wafers sold as bondable consumables
idea: Stimulus 'coffee pod' -> a dedicated, EUV-free line makes only the storage-element layer (dense capacitor or bit-element array on a thin carrier) and ships it as a consumable that logic or periphery fabs hybrid-bond face-to-face onto their CMOS wafers. Each layer runs on the cheapest line suited to it.
why: Splits DRAM capital: the bit-element fab needs no EUV transistor layers (fact 4) and the ~49% periphery runs in logic fabs (fact 7); claimed 30-40% capex per bit reduction and a U.S. entry point.

title: Hula hoop: persistent supercurrent loops at liquid-nitrogen temperature
idea: Stimulus 'hula hoop' (keeps circling once started) -> store a flux quantum in a YBCO nanoloop with a weak link, operated in a 77 K liquid-nitrogen rack memory pool rather than a helium cryostat; current circulates indefinitely and a nearby flux sensor reads its direction.
why: Zero-leakage, zero-refresh storage (fact 3) with aJ switching energy (fact 10), and avoids helium (Qatar supply offline) by using abundant LN2 for pooled memory.

title: Honeycomb: anodized alumina pores template 500:1 capacitors, no plasma
idea: Stimulus 'honeycomb' -> anodize an aluminum film in oxalic acid so it self-organizes into hexagonal pores (40-60 nm pitch, AR up to 500:1), guided by a nanoimprinted pre-dent, then ALD TiN (from TiCl4/NH3) and ZrO2/Al2O3 into the pores. The electrolyte digs the holes: no fluorocarbon etch, no NF3 chamber clean.
why: Breaks the 60-75:1 AR wall toward >115:1 (fact 1) and removes the capacitor-hole EUV/etch step (fact 4); ~2x Cs or half the footprint, fluorine-free.

title: Pencil lead: carbon mold capacitors released by dry ash, no HF
idea: Stimulus 'pencil lead' -> build the capacitor mold from amorphous carbon instead of oxide, etch holes with O2/SO2 plasma, deposit the electrodes, then remove the mold by oxygen ashing. Today the oxide mold is stripped in liquid HF whose capillary forces topple tall cylinders; a dry ash has no capillary force at all.
why: Removes the pattern-collapse limit so pillars can reach the ~115:1 AR needed for more charge (fact 1); eliminates HF and C4F8 from the capacitor module with existing tools.

title: Bamboo forest: grow capacitor pillars upward instead of etching them
idea: Stimulus 'bamboo forest' (tall shoots grow up, nobody carves them) -> pattern a thin Al2O3 mask with BCl3/Cl2, then grow vertical Si/SiGe nanopillars by selective-area epitaxy (SiH4/HCl) to 100:1 and convert them into bottom electrodes with chloride-ALD TiN. Height comes from growth time, not a deep fluorocarbon etch.
why: Decouples pillar aspect ratio from etch physics (fact 1) and drops the hardest etch/EUV layer (fact 4); fluorine-free end to end.

title: Pottery glaze: nanoscale barrier-layer giant-k capacitor dielectric
idea: Stimulus 'glazed pottery' (conductive body, insulating skin) -> build the dielectric from 3-5 nm oxygen-deficient TiO2-x grains each wrapped in a ~1 nm Al2O3 skin by alternating chloride/organometallic ALD; charge piles up at the many thin internal barriers (the CaCu3Ti4O12 trick) for an effective k of several hundred.
why: Exceeds the k~70 needed (fact 1), allowing near-planar capacitors with AR <20:1 and fewer deep-etch steps (fact 4); fluorine-free chemistry.

title: Borax box: boron-aluminum nitride ferroelectric from U.S. boron, no scandium
idea: Stimulus 'borax laundry box' (mined in Boron, California) -> sputter wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N ferroelectric (remanent polarization ~100 uC/cm^2, ~5-10x HZO) from Al/B targets in N2/Ar and pattern it with Cl2/BCl3; use it as a planar storage capacitor or ferroelectric gate. No hafnium, scandium or fluorine.
why: ~10x charge per area enables a planar storage element (fact 1) built from abundant domestic boron and aluminum (scarce-resource and U.S. manufacturability axes).

title: Sugar cube: croconic-acid proton ferroelectric replaces fluoropolymer PVDF
idea: Stimulus 'sugar cube' (a crystal of small organic molecules) -> vapor-deposit croconic acid, a hydrogen-bonded organic ferroelectric (~20 uC/cm^2, highest among organics) whose polarization flips by proton transfer along H-bonds, as the storage layer of a BEOL cell at <150 C. It replaces PVDF-TrFE, the standard organic ferroelectric, which is a fluoropolymer.
why: Low-temperature, fluorine-free nonvolatile storage layer that can be stacked over periphery in tiers (fact 2); proton-transfer switching is fast and low-voltage (fact 10).

title: Seesaw: negative-capacitance layer amplifies the storage capacitor
idea: Stimulus 'seesaw' (push one end down, the other rises) -> place a 3 nm ZrO2-based ferroelectric, biased in its negative-capacitance region, in series with an Al2O3/ZrO2 storage dielectric, all ALD from ZrCl4 and TMA/H2O; the dielectric stabilizes the stack so it shows no hysteresis while net capacitance exceeds the dielectric alone.
why: Raises Cs ~1.5-2x at the same AR (fact 1) or lets the array voltage drop for the same charge (fact 10); chloride/organometallic ALD only, no fluorine.

title: Kitchen sponge: electrodeposited MnO2 pseudocapacitive storage node
idea: Stimulus 'kitchen sponge' (soaks up far more than its surface suggests) -> coat the storage node with ~3 nm MnO2 grown by aqueous electrodeposition from a manganese sulfate bath, with a thin hydrated ZrO2 proton conductor as solid electrolyte; surface Mn3+/Mn4+ redox stores ~10-50x the charge of a dielectric of equal area.
why: A planar ~30 nm^2 pad stores ~5 fF-equivalent charge, replacing 70:1 pillars (fact 1) and deep etch/EUV (fact 4); abundant Mn, fluorine-free aqueous bath.

title: Ice sculpture: frozen ionomer double layer locks the gate charge
idea: Stimulus 'ice sculpture' (shape fixed while frozen) -> gate a gain-cell transistor with a nanodot of high-Tg sodium polystyrene-sulfonate ionomer instead of the usual TFSI/PF6/BF4 fluorinated ionic liquids; an embedded nanoheater softens it for ~20 ns while the gate field forms an electric double layer, then cooling freezes the ions, shifting threshold by >1 V.
why: Retention set by frozen ions rather than junction leakage (fact 3); large Vt signal allows tiny cells without a capacitor (fact 1); avoids every fluorinated electrolyte salt.

title: Origami scroll: self-rolling nanoscroll capacitor released by plain water
idea: Stimulus 'paper scroll' -> deposit a flat, strain-graded TiN/Al2O3/TiN stack on a water-soluble GeO2 sacrificial layer; dissolving the GeO2 in DI water (instead of HF) lets built-in strain roll the stack into a ~10-turn, ~100 nm diameter nanoscroll over its contact, giving pillar-class electrode area from planar deposition.
why: 3D capacitor area without deep high-AR etch (facts 1, 4); fluorine-free release that also avoids wet-etch pillar collapse.

title: Sticky note: stiction itself becomes the bit in fluorine-free NEMS
idea: Stimulus 'sticky note' (sticks, peels, re-sticks) -> a TiN nano-cantilever is either stuck to its pad by van der Waals adhesion (1) or freed by a thermal-bimorph or repulsive electrostatic kick (0), read by contact current. MEMS normally fights stiction with fluorinated anti-stiction monolayers and releases with HF vapor or XeF2; here an amorphous-carbon sacrificial layer is ashed in O2 and stiction is the feature.
why: Zero-power nonvolatile mechanical bit with no leakage (fact 3), no capacitor (fact 1), stackable in BEOL (fact 2); no fluorinated release or coating chemistry.

title: Mood ring: fluorine-free ferroelectric nematic fluid in nanowells
idea: Stimulus 'mood ring' (liquid crystal that changes state) -> fill 20 nm wells with an RM734-class ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (a polar fluid with ~6 uC/cm^2 and no fluorine, unlike most display LCs); a field pulse flips the polar director up or down and boundary anchoring holds it, read as a polarization current or capacitance. A fluid self-heals, so there are no fatigue-causing defects.
why: Fatigue-free polar storage with low switching voltage (fact 10) and no refresh (fact 3), filled by capillary action with no etch (fact 4).

title: Rust: hematite antiferromagnet switched by orbital torque, no heavy metals
idea: Stimulus 'rust' -> use alpha-Fe2O3 (hematite), an insulating antiferromagnet, as the bit: its Neel vector is rotated by orbital-Hall torque from a light Ti or Cr layer instead of Pt or W spin-Hall metals, and read by spin-Hall magnetoresistance. Stacks are sputtered and Ar-ion-milled, so no fluorine etch.
why: Nonvolatile, ps-switching, field-immune bit with no refresh (fact 3) and immunity to row-hammer coupling (fact 9), made from iron oxide and avoiding tungsten (China ~80%) and platinum-group metals.

title: Layer cake: lateral capacitors carved by HCl vapor in Si/SiGe stacks
idea: Stimulus 'layer cake' -> grow a 32-tier Si/SiGe superlattice, cut one vertical slot with Cl2/HBr, recess the SiGe layers sideways with highly selective HCl vapor to form horizontal pockets, and line each pocket with chloride-ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN to make lateral capacitors stacked like cake layers.
why: Delivers the 26+ tiers needed for 3D DRAM breakeven (fact 2) with one litho step for many tiers (fact 4), with no fluorocarbon etch and no HF.

title: Seashell nacre: titania nanosheets self-stack into a k~125 dielectric
idea: Stimulus 'nacre' (layered bricks of mineral) -> exfoliate Ti0.87O2 nanosheets in water with tetrabutylammonium hydroxide and deposit them layer by layer by Langmuir-Blodgett at room temperature, giving a ~5 nm dielectric with k~125 and low leakage; no plasma, no fluorinated surfactants.
why: k~125 exceeds the k~70 needed (fact 1), letting capacitor AR fall to ~40:1; room-temperature aqueous deposition lowers tool capex (fact 4).

title: Breathing lung: brownmillerite oxide inhales oxygen to switch whole-volume
idea: Stimulus 'lungs' -> a 10 nm SrFeO2.5 brownmillerite layer topotactically 'inhales' oxygen from an adjacent Ta2O5 reservoir under +1 V to become metallic SrFeO3, and exhales it at -1 V; the whole volume switches (not a filament), giving ~1000x resistance change with tight cell-to-cell spread.
why: Volume switching removes the variability tail of filamentary ReRAM while staying nonvolatile with no refresh (fact 3); iron-based oxides deposited without fluorine.

title: Dam: GaN/AlGaN potential well holds stored charge for days
idea: Stimulus 'hydro dam' (water held behind a tall wall) -> store the bit as electrons in an AlGaN/GaN 2DEG pocket behind a 3.4 eV-gap barrier and read it through a gain transistor; leakage falls exponentially with bandgap, so retention reaches hours to days. GaN is grown by MOCVD and etched with Cl2/BCl3, with no fluorine.
why: Shrinks the leakage tail >1000x vs silicon (fact 3) so refresh becomes rare; capacitorless gain-cell read (fact 1).

title: Pool chlorine tablet: MoCl5-grown molybdenum electrodes replace WF6 tungsten
idea: Stimulus 'pool chlorine tablet' -> deposit storage-node contacts, landing pads and plate electrodes as molybdenum by ALD/CVD from MoCl5 or MoO2Cl2 plus H2 instead of tungsten from WF6; Mo has lower resistivity in narrow features and needs no TiN barrier. Molybdenum is mined in Colorado and Arizona.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6 from the cell (scarce-resource axis); barrier-less contacts free ~2 nm per side for a larger capacitor (fact 1).

title: Weathervane: surface-anchored dipolar molecular rotors with nitrile dipoles
idea: Stimulus 'weathervane' (points one way until pushed) -> a monolayer of tripod-anchored molecular rotors whose paddle carries a strong nitrile/nitro dipole (not the usual fluorinated dipole groups), designed with two detents 180 degrees apart; a gate field flips the paddles and the collective dipole shifts a FET threshold by ~0.3 V.
why: Molecular-scale (~1 nm^2) nonvolatile bit with nondestructive read (fact 8) and no capacitor (fact 1), deposited from solution at room temperature (fact 4).

title: Organic food label: certified fluorine-free memory gets procurement and permit advantage
idea: Stimulus 'organic food label' -> create a U.S. 'PFAS-free memory' certification (no PFAS resists or surfactants, no fluorinated etch or clean, no WF6) tied to federal procurement preference and fast-track water permits, because fluorine-free fabs skip PFAS wastewater treatment and clear the coming EU PFAS restriction. It pulls the fluorine-free storage elements in this cell into early demand.
why: Turns the constraint into market access and faster fab siting (capital and time chokepoints); estimated $100M+ abatement capex avoided per fab and EU export de-risked.

title: Photo film: silver-bromide latent-image speck as an atom-scale bit
idea: Stimulus 'silver-halide film' -> a 10 nm AgBr nanocrystal between two electrodes: an electron pulse nucleates a 4-atom Ag cluster (the photographic latent image) at a sensitivity site, making the crystal tunnel-conductive; an oxidizing pulse dissolves it. Bromide chemistry, no fluorine.
why: Few-atom motion promises lower energy and variability than filamentary ReRAM; nonvolatile so no refresh (fact 3); low-temperature halide deposition fits BEOL tiers (fact 2).

title: Toothpaste without fluoride: hydroxyapatite OH-column dipole order stores bits
idea: Stimulus 'fluoride toothpaste', inverted -> use hydroxyapatite (the fluoride-free tooth mineral) thin films, whose columns of OH- ions can order head-to-tail into a polar state; a field pulse reverses the OH column orientation, read as a polarization or capacitance change. Calcium phosphate comes from Florida phosphate rock.
why: Earth-abundant, U.S.-sourced nonvolatile polar storage layer (scarce-resource axis) with low switching voltage from proton/OH reorientation (fact 10).

title: Hand warmer: undercooled liquid tin nanodot versus solid tin
idea: Stimulus 'click-disc hand warmer' (supercooled liquid that crystallizes on a click) -> tin nanodots embedded in SiO2 (formed by thermal dewetting, no etch) can stay liquid ~150 K below their 232 C melting point; a Joule pulse melts a dot (1) and a sharp field or acoustic 'click' nucleates crystallization (0). Liquid tin is ~3x more resistive than solid, read nondestructively.
why: A new phase-memory class with no amorphous drift and tiny nanoscale latent heat, nonvolatile within the undercooling window (fact 3); fluorine-free dewetting fabrication.
